# @thednp/rpc

## 0.4.0 — read this if you are upgrading from 0.3.x

- **Cross-origin protection is ON BY DEFAULT and it will break headerless clients.** `origin: "self"` now applies without configuration. A request with neither `Origin` nor `Sec-Fetch-Site` is `403` — that means `curl` and native clients. Set `allowHeaderless: true` if you want them. A browser's native `<form>` navigation sends `Origin`, so it is checked like any other request; use a per-function `fallback` for the no-JS flow. An array `origin` **widens** `"self"` rather than replacing it, and there is deliberately no `trustProxy` option.
- **Bodies over 10 MiB are `413`** by default (`bodyLimit`, `0` disables). Registering a framework parser does not replace it.
- **Validation is opt-in and runs before your handler**, on both the HTTP path and a direct call. A rejected input is **`422`**, not `400`; production keeps each issue's `path` and any author-written `hint`, and drops only the validator library's own `message`.
- **`wiki/migration.md`** covers both directions: upgrading an existing 0.3.x install (nothing was removed from the option types, but two defaults changed and one surfaces as a `403` or a `413`) and coming from Next.js/TanStack Start/SvelteKit/tRPC/Telefunc, with a symptom-to-cause table. Point users there rather than re-explaining the migration.
- `dist/` is rebuilt; `pnpm check:ts5` type-checks the examples under a pinned TypeScript 5.9.3 and is **not** part of `pnpm lint`, because it only resolves while the examples point at this repo.

Vite plugin for automatic RPC generation from server functions. One module (`src/api/server.ts`), two resolutions: real functions on SSR/Node, fetch stubs in the browser. Types flow through because tsc sees the source module — only the Vite bundler swaps the implementation.

## Core API
- `createServerFunction(name, handler, options?)` — define a server function: `(signal: AbortSignal, input)`, where input is a single JSON-serializable value (or `FormData` for `multipart/form-data` functions). `TResult` is constrained to `JsonValue | void` at the factory and on `ServerFunctionInit` (fire-and-forget `void` returns are allowed); everything client-side (`ClientFunction`, `getClientStub`'s `R`) leaves the result open so `interface` results work — only `getClientStub`'s *input* is constrained, since that is what the client serializes. A handler taking no input keeps a zero-parameter stub (`fn()`)
- `import { fn } from "./api"` — on the server calls the real handler, in the browser calls auto-generated `fetch` stubs
- Returns `{ data: Promise<T>, cancel: (reason: string) => void }`
- Options: `{ method: "GET" | "POST", contentType: "application/json" | "text/plain" | "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" | "multipart/form-data", credentials, rpcPrefix, schema, hint, hints }`
- **Multi-prefix**: `rpcPrefix` (default `"__rpc"` via the exported `defaultPrefix` constant) registers the function in a prefix-scoped map (`getFunctionsForPrefix(prefix)`). Same names can coexist under different prefixes (versioned/namespaced APIs); middleware dispatches to the prefix-scoped map; the plugin generates client stubs per prefix. See `wiki/multi-prefix-guide.md`
- **`schema.from(vendorSchema)`** — transparent identity wrapper used as a TypeScript *inference boundary*. `createServerFunction` infers the handler's parameter with `InferOutput<TSchema>`, a structural match against the schema's own type, and a heavy vendor graph (measured: arktype `.narrow()` and its function pipes) exceeds the instantiation budget older TypeScript allows — the call then fails with `TS2589` on TS 5.x and passes on TS 7.x. The budget is per inference site, so `from` splits one expensive inference into two cheap ones: the deep match happens at `from` and the overload only ever sees `StandardSchemaV1<in, out>`. It validates and converts nothing (the same object comes back), so a non-conforming schema still fails loudly at the first call rather than being laundered. Type-only. Not needed for rpc's own builder
- **Typed error subclasses** — `NotFoundError(message, hint, data?)` → `404`/`NOT_FOUND`, `ForbiddenError(message, hint, data?)` → `403`/`FORBIDDEN`, `ConflictError(message, hint, data?)` → `409`/`CONFLICT`, all extending `RPCError` and carrying a `status`, so an adapter answers that status instead of a `500`. `hint` is **required** on the subclasses because a class whose purpose is to explain a failure should not be constructible without the explanation
- **`RPCError(message, code?, data?, hint?)`** — `hint` is developer-facing advice about how to fix the failure, dev-only like `code`/`data`. In development the 4xx body is `{ error, code, data?, hint? }`; in production it collapses to the status reason phrase (`"Not Found"`, not the author's message)
- **Client field-error helpers** (`@thednp/rpc/helpers`) — `fieldErrors(err)` → `Record<string, string[]>` keyed by the rendered path, `fieldErrorText(err, field)` → that field's messages joined or `""`, `fieldErrorHint(err, field)` → the field's hint falling back to the function-wide one. Validator-agnostic: the server normalises every library's issues into `{ path, message?, hint? }`, so the same three lines render a zod, valibot, arktype or effect rejection. **All three work in production**, where an issue has no `message` and the helpers fall back to the hint; an issue with neither still appears as a key with empty text, which is enough to mark an input invalid — so a `""` from `fieldErrorText` can mean "no hint was written", not "the field passed"
- **`onDispatch(ctx)`** (middleware option) — one `DispatchContext` per dispatch, after the response settles, whatever the outcome. Carries `id`, `prefix`, `functionName`, `registeredNames` (turns "Function not found" into "did you mean"), `originTier` (which cross-origin tier decided), `method` vs `declaredMethod`, declared vs actual `contentType`, `argShape`, `status`, `outcome`, `error`, `durationMs`. **The library retains nothing** — no buffer, ring or TTL; the app owns storage. `argShape` describes arguments and never captures values, bounded in depth/keys and cycle-safe. The correlation `id` is placed on failure bodies only, and only when a hook is registered, so the default error body is byte-for-byte unchanged. A throwing hook is ignored
- **`schema` option (input validation)** — accepts any [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev) (zod, valibot, arktype, effect `Schema`, or rpc's builder). A rejection is **`422`**, never `400`: `400` now means only that the request could not be understood, so a client can tell a malformed request from a rejected one by status alone. **Production keeps each issue's `path` and any `hint` the author wrote, and drops the validator library's `message`** — because some libraries interpolate the value that failed into their default message (measured through `~standard.validate` with `name: 12345`: valibot → `"Invalid type: Expected string but received 12345"`, zod → `"Invalid input: expected string, received number"`, arktype → `"name must be a string (was a number)"`). So safety depends on the library, which is why it is withheld structurally; a `path` is safe because the caller supplied the field and a `hint` is safe because the author wrote it. An author with no `hints` still gets *which* field failed. **Never encode an existence check in a schema** — `~standard.validate` may be async, so a refinement that hits the database would put "already registered" on the wire; do it in the handler and throw one neutral error, or a login enumerates accounts.
- **No validator dependency** — `schema({ email: field.string({ hint }), name: optional(field.string()), tags: array(field.string()) })`, plus `field.number` (rejects `NaN`/`Infinity`), `field.boolean`, `nullable`, `record`, and `field.custom(inner)` to wrap any Standard Schema as a leaf. **Structural only — no `transform`, no coercion.** It is also the strict one: it **rejects** unknown keys, where zod strips them and valibot/arktype ignore them (measured on the same input). Prefer a real library when you need coercion
- **Limits** — the `schema` validates the call's single input; there is no second argument for it to miss (a handler declaring more than `(signal, input)` is a type error). A nojs `<form>` fallback should use a per-function `fallback` with `schema`, whose `422` becomes a `303` HTML redirect carrying `__flash` — a bare schema rejection cannot re-render HTML with errors; a heavy vendor type (arktype `.narrow()`) can exhaust the inference budget and fail with `TS2589` on TS 5.x — annotate it `StandardSchemaV1<I, O>` to collapse the walk (type-only, runtime unchanged). Since 0.4.0, a `schema` failure is `422` while a malformed body is `400`.
- **Where to throw** — throwable typed error, exported from `@thednp/rpc/server` (as is `formatError`); throw for server-side failures only. For expected user-facing problems, either pass a `schema` (a `422` at the boundary, rendered as a `303` `__flash` redirect for a native `<form>` with `fallback`) or return `{ error }` (a `200` carrying the outcome) — the two are different wire contracts, and migrating between them changes the client's control flow, not just its body. Dev 500 body: `{ error, code, data }`; prod: generic `{ error: "Internal Server Error" }` only. Client rejection `message` = the error string
- `provideRequestContext(init, cb)` / `getRequestContext()` — per-request `AsyncLocalStorage` context available to all server function code; `RequestEvent` includes `nativeEvent`, `locals`, adapter-bound `redirect`, and staged `header(name, value)` (rides the `{ data }` send, a `send`/`redirect` short-circuit, the fallback `303`, or an error response); works across Express/Fastify/Hono/Koa/h3
- `unwrapEnvelope<T>(json)` — client helper from `@thednp/rpc/helpers` to unwrap the `{ data }` wire protocol envelope; for native HTTP clients (Deno, Bun, curl-equivalents) that don't use the auto-generated fetch stubs. Same error contract as `handleResponse`: a **top-level** `error` (including `403`/`422`/`409` alongside `400`/`404`/`405`/`415`/`500`) throws; `{ data: { error } }` resolves normally (validation-as-data). Status-code agnostic — keep the `res.ok` check. `RPCError` is server-side only (`@thednp/rpc/server`), not a client export, and its `code`/`data` are stripped in production regardless
- `resolveRPCPrefix(rpcPrefix?)` from `@thednp/rpc/server` — the single prefix-resolution point used by all five adapters: explicit argument → the prefix published by `setGlobalPrefix`/`loadRPCConfig` → the `"__rpc"` default. `createServerFunction` resolves the same way, so a function always registers under the prefix the middleware dispatches on. Call it if you build a custom adapter or wrapper and need to agree with the built-in ones
  - **`fallback` — the built-in no-JS `<form>` flow.** Set it on a function and a
    native form submission is answered with a `303` and the failure flashed,
    instead of a JSON body. `{ to, replay? }`, a bare path, or a function per
    outcome. `replay` defaults to **empty** — a URL reaches history, `Referer` and
    access logs, so only named fields come back. Detection is whether the request
    is a **document navigation**, not its content type: a form-declared function is
    called by two clients that both send form encodings, so `Sec-Fetch-Dest` /
    `Sec-Fetch-Mode` decide, falling back to `Accept: text/html`. A `fetch` from the
    generated stub still gets its `422`; a JSON-declared function still gets `415`;
    an unexpected throw still gets `500`. `to` is root-relative only, so it cannot
    become an open redirect — for an off-origin target call `redirect()` from the
    request context, which takes precedence. Because it runs inside the dispatch it
    *is* subject to the origin check, unlike an app-layer middleware mounted before
    it (which is a CSRF hole). Full page: `wiki/nojs-fallback.md`.
  - `FLASH_PARAM` / `encodeFormFlash` / `decodeFormFlash` from
    **`@thednp/rpc/flash`** — read a flash in the browser. A client-safe entry
    (`@thednp/rpc/server` is not), because a no-JS fallback has to be read on both
    sides of the wire; the codec imports nothing. Capped at 4 KiB, dropped rather
    than truncated past that, since the browser re-requests the redirect URL and it
    becomes a request line.
- Registered function names become URL paths: `POST /{prefix}/{name}` with body `JSON.stringify(args)`

## Wire Protocol (client module → server)
- **POST (default):** `/{prefix}/{fnName}` body = `JSON.stringify([input])` (bare JSON array wrapping the single input, not `{data:[...]}`)
- **text/plain** POST: body = `args[0]` as raw string
- **application/x-www-form-urlencoded** POST: body = `new URLSearchParams(args[0]).toString()` (single object arg; server parses back to an object of strings via `URLSearchParams`)
- **multipart/form-data** POST: client sends the `FormData` passed as the first argument (browser sets the boundary). Server-side, parse before the handler runs — framework multipart middleware BEFORE the RPC middleware (multer, @fastify/multipart, koa-body, hono formData) and the parsed fields object becomes the function argument; without a parser the handler gets `{ raw: "<body>" }`, which you must parse yourself (busboy or formidable — Node has no built-in multipart parser)
- **GET:** `/{prefix}/{fnName}?args=encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify([input]))`
- **Response:** always `{ data: <result> }` — 200 wraps everything, even `{ error }` responses (they resolve as data, not thrown)
- **Status codes:** 200 (success or validation-as-data), `400` (malformed request), `403`/`404`/`405`/`409`/`413`/`415`/`500`, and **`422` for a schema rejection** (all transport errors → data promise rejects). 400 = GET `?args=` present but not a JSON array. 415 = request Content-Type doesn't match the function's declared contentType (json/text strict; form functions accept either form encoding, but a JSON-declared function does **not** accept form bodies — leniency is one-directional; headerless requests exempt). 500 body: generic `{ error: "Internal Server Error" }` in production; dev includes the message (and `code`/`data` for `RPCError`)
- See `wiki/wire-protocol.md` for full curl examples

## Config
- `rpc.config.ts` imports `defineConfig` from `@thednp/rpc/config` (vite-free subpath — safe for serverless bundles): `defineConfig({ rpcPrefix: "__rpc", serverFiles: "exact" | "glob", scanRoot, silent })` — note there is no `adapter` option: the adapter is the subpath you import (`@thednp/rpc/express`, `/hono`, `/koa`, `/h3`, `/fastify`)
- `serverFiles: "exact" | "glob"` — `"exact"` (default) matches `server.ts|js|mjs|mts`; `"glob"` recursively matches `*.server.{ts,js,mjs,mts}` under the scan root
- `scanRoot: string` — scan directory (default `<root>/src/api`); point it at a shared package in monorepos
- `silent: boolean` — suppress the `NO_CONFIG_FOUND` warning when no config file is found. Useful for wrapper plugins that define server functions directly without a config file
- `loadRPCConfig(configFile?, opts?)` — loads config programmatically. `configFile` is an optional path; when omitted the config-file search runs. Pass `{ silent: true }` as the **second** argument to suppress the `NO_CONFIG_FOUND` warning, or as the sole argument — both `loadRPCConfig(undefined, { silent: true })` and `loadRPCConfig({ silent: true })` are accepted. It also publishes the resolved prefix via `setGlobalPrefix`, and every adapter resolves its prefix the same way (explicit argument → global prefix → `"__rpc"`), so registration and dispatch cannot disagree. A config file that fails to load falls back to the defaults with a warning. Still recommended: `createRPCMiddleware({ rpcPrefix: config.rpcPrefix })`
- `createRPCMiddleware({ origin, allowHeaderless })` — cross-origin check, **on by default** (`origin: "self"`), so a foreign `Origin` is `403` without any configuration. `origin` accepts `"self"`, a string, or an **allowlist array**; a list *widens* self rather than replacing it, so naming an extra origin can never lock you out of your own site. Three tiers, first signal with meaning wins: (1) `Origin` present → the policy decides; `"self"` compares the origin's **host and port** against `Host`, with *default* ports normalised (`https://app.example.com:443` matches `Host: app.example.com`), so TLS termination needs no action but a proxy that rewrites `Host` to another port 403s every check — preserve `Host` (Vite `preview.proxy` needs `changeOrigin: false`) or name the public origin in `origin`, while a lookalike like `https://app.example.com.evil.com` and `Origin: null` are rejected; an explicit list matches exactly; (2) `Origin` absent but `Sec-Fetch-Site` present → allow only `same-origin`/`none`, else 403 (a proxy that strips `Origin` can no longer turn the check into a no-op); (3) both absent → **403 unless `allowHeaderless: true`**, which is the opt-in for `curl` and server-to-server calls. A browser's native `<form>` navigation supplies `Origin`, so the built-in no-JS fallback is checked normally. `Origin` deliberately short-circuits ahead of `Sec-Fetch-Site` so an allowlisted sibling's `same-site` request still passes. **No forwarded header is ever trusted** — `X-Forwarded-Host` is not consulted and there is no `trustProxy` option; an ingress that rewrites `Host` is fixed by naming the public origin in `origin`. The rule lives once in `isOriginRequestAllowed` (`src/server-helpers.ts`), used by all five adapters. **Breaking in 0.4.0:** the check was opt-in and off by default before, so `curl`/native clients now need `allowHeaderless: true`; `isOriginRequestAllowed` also changed from three positional args to one `OriginCheck` object. `isOriginAllowed` (literal match) and `isSelfOrigin` (host and port) remain exported as building blocks
- `createRPCMiddleware({ bodyLimit })` — request body cap in bytes, default `10485760` (10 MiB), `0` disables. Applies to the paths rpc reads itself: `readStream` (express/fastify/koa) and `readWebBody` (hono/h3). Do not assume a host framework's limit covers this — `express.json({ limit })` only limits the content types it claims and *declines* urlencoded and multipart, leaving them on the stream for rpc to read uncapped (measured: a 20 MB multipart POST returned `200` buffered in full before the cap existed). A `Content-Length` pre-check is NOT sufficient: a `Request` built in JavaScript carries no `Content-Length` (absent for chunked bodies), so the cap is enforced against the bytes as they arrive. Enforced while streaming, never after buffering; past the cap the remainder is drained and discarded up to a ceiling so the `413` is deliverable. **Fastify is effectively exempt** — its content-type parser runs before any hook, so either Fastify's own `bodyLimit` answers (`413 FST_ERR_CTP_BODY_TOO_LARGE`) or it answers `415 FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_MEDIA_TYPE` itself; set Fastify's `bodyLimit`, not this one. Per-adapter table in wiki/security.md#body-size-limits. **Hono's two buffered-body paths are the exception and cannot be capped**, because rpc never reads them: `@hono/node-server` decodes onto `c.env.incoming`, and a host middleware that already read the body leaves it in Hono's `c.req.bodyCache` (a common pattern — an auth step calling `c.req.json()`). Note the cache is keyed by *body form* and `c.req.json()` stores **raw text** under `text`, parsing it itself, so dispatch on the form: raw text goes through `parseRawBody` against the declared type, an already-parsed value through `preParsedBody`. Until 0.4.0 Hono's declared-JSON path bypassed the cap entirely via `c.req.json()` (measured: 4 KB at `bodyLimit: 64` gave Hono `200` and h3 `413`); JSON is what every client stub sends, and it survived at 100% coverage because the Hono suite had no `bodyLimit` test
- Plugin options in `vite.config.ts` (`rpc()`) override `rpc.config.ts` in dev only
- Config discovery: `rpc.config.ts` > `.js` > `.mjs` > `.mts` > `.rpcrc.ts` > `.rpcrc.js`

## Project Structure
- `src/api/server.ts` — server functions (auto-scanned). Aliases: `server.js`, `.mjs`, `.mts`; glob mode matches `*.server.{ts,js,mjs,mts}`
- `src/api/index.ts` — `export * from "./server"` (single import point for SSR + client — types flow through this)
- SSR: `src/entry-server.ts` (imports real functions) and `src/entry-client.ts` (imports fetch stubs)
- SPA: just import from `./api` in client code
- Example apps: `examples/` — `spa`, `express`, `fastify`, `h3`, `hono`, `koa`, `ssr` (plain RPC + DOM update), plus `react-query` and `solid-query` (show `@tanstack/*-query` integration on top of RPC), plus `advanced` (Express multi-prefix `public:rpc`/`admin:rpc` + universal middleware)

## Rules
- First handler argument is always `(signal: AbortSignal, input)` — one input, never positional args
- Handler input must be JSON-serializable (string, number, boolean, null, array, plain object) — or a `FormData` instance as the single input of a `multipart/form-data` function
- Do NOT pass DOM nodes, functions, class instances, or circular refs
- Export functions individually (named exports). No default export or bundled objects
- Re-export from `src/api/index.ts` — this is non-negotiable for SSR/client duality

## Security Boundaries
- Prefix regex: `new RegExp("^/" + escapeRegExp(prefix) + "/")` — not `startsWith` (prevents segment bypass like `/__rpc-evil/foo`)
- Default POST methods — CSRF-safe (no `<img>`/form GET can trigger mutations)
- Content-Type enforcement — mismatched content types get 415 (json/text strict; forms interoperable; headerless exempt)
- 404s are generic (no function name echoed); status code still distinguishes unknown (404) from known (405/415/403) — names ship in the client bundle so are not secret
- 500s: always generic (no message/stack leak); dev mode includes `RPCError` payloads (`code`/`data`) only
- Duplicate function names: throw in dev, warn + keep first in production
- Auth and rate limiting: middleware-host, registered before `createRPCMiddleware()`; origin checks are built into all adapters and on by default
- Body limits: rpc's own streaming `bodyLimit` (10 MiB default) on the bodies it reads itself, in addition to host-framework parsers; Fastify is effectively host-limited

## Development Scripts
- `pnpm test` — run tests once with coverage (`vitest run --coverage`); project aims for 100% coverage on all metrics
- `pnpm test:watch` — run tests in watch mode with coverage
- `pnpm test:ui` — run tests with UI
- `pnpm test:dev` — run examples in dev mode (scripts/dev-test)
- `pnpm test:prod` — run examples in prod preview (scripts/dev-test --mode=preview)
- `pnpm lint` — lint + typecheck (`deno lint src` + `tsc -noEmit`)
- `pnpm format` — `deno fmt src tests examples/**/src`
- `pnpm clean` — remove build artifacts and caches
- `pnpm build` — tsdown bundle (outputs to `dist/`)

## Wiki Pages (in learning order)
- `wiki/quickstart.md` — Rebuild the Express SSR example from `create-vite` in under a minute
- `wiki/getting-started.md` — Installation, project structure, auto-scanning, and your first function
- `wiki/configuration.md` — `rpc.config.ts`, `vite.config.ts`, `loadRPCConfig`
- `wiki/server-functions.md` — `createServerFunction` API, methods, content types (JSON/text/urlencoded/multipart), input validation (the `schema` option — Standard Schema across zod/valibot/arktype/effect, plus rpc's dependency-free builder; the dev-vs-production body contract, `hint`/`hints`, the first-argument-only limit, and validation-as-data as the alternative), typed errors (`RPCError`), AbortSignal, request context (`RequestEvent`, `send`, `header`, `functionName`)
- `wiki/multi-prefix-guide.md` — Parallel RPC instances: versioned/public/admin API layouts, per-prefix middleware, canary deployments, origin validation per instance
- `wiki/middleware.md` — Universal adapter-agnostic middleware via the request context (`locals` bridge, `getRequestMeta`, `sendResponse` short-circuits, `header` staging, wrapping official framework middleware), and `onDispatch` for observing every dispatch (the library retains nothing; `argShape` never captures argument values)
- `wiki/nojs-fallback.md` — Progressive enhancement: making an RPC endpoint work as a no-JS `<form>` action (detection rule, shared validation, PRG 303 redirects, state recovery)
- `wiki/client-usage.md` — Generated client modules, type safety, error handling, multipart uploads, `@tanstack/react-query` integration, and an SSR gotcha for disabled queries (solid-query hangs `renderToStringAsync`; use `queryClient.fetchQuery()` on submit instead)
- `wiki/wire-protocol.md` — HTTP contract: request/response bodies, status codes, curl debugging
- `wiki/adapters.md` — Express, Fastify, Hono, Koa, h3 (`attachRPC`, `attachVite`, body limits, `viteMiddleware` for Fastify/Hono/h3, Hono header fallback in `getRequestMeta`)
- `wiki/security.md` — Prefix guards, method enforcement, origin, CSRF hardening
- `wiki/comparison.md` — Cross-origin/CSRF boundary vs Next.js Server Actions, TanStack Start, SvelteKit, tRPC, and Vike/Telefunc. Framed as *secure by default, strictest-once-configured, multi-origin without a proxy*: with `origin` set, rpc rejects an untrusted `Origin` even when `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` claims otherwise, which TanStack's tier order waves through (measured 3 stricter / 2 more lenient, both lenient cases deliberate). `Where the trade costs you` keeps the real sharp edges — case-sensitive origin matching, literal origins only, opt-in-only input validation (`schema`) whose detail is stripped in production, deliberate `Referer` omission Re-verified against vendor source and docs on 2026-09-27 (Next.js 16.3.6, TanStack Start 1.168.59, SvelteKit 2.70.3, tRPC 11.18.0, Telefunc 0.2.24) — an earlier draft wrongly claimed Next.js aborts requests with no `Origin`; it lets them through, the fail-open posture rpc had before 0.4.0.
- `wiki/best-practices.md` — Auth middleware, rate limiting, per-function authorization, body limits
